column1: # CEOS-APPROX SWEEP (2026-09-24): an older hexapole-corrected column -- CEOS CESCOR-like, tuned at 30 mrad -- opened
# past its design with the probe known. Can a widespread instrument still give depth-resolved ptychography by tanking
# its aberrations? Tableau: campaign/aberration_waves.py ceos_tableau (A5 = 1.0 mm from CEOS; every other term
# unsourced, 0.1 waves). C5 = 1 mm fixed throughout, as in the round sweep. aber_json is always generated, never typed.
#   round_a<A>    the controls: the round sweep's own balance (plan_probe.py), 4 A probe, re-simulated because the
#   ceosopt_a<A>  THE SWEEP. The operator fights for the smallest probe: hardware A5, A4, B4 fixed; A1 A2 S3 A3 D4
#                 retuned at this aperture to 0.1 waves; C1, C3 and coma B2 (set against B4, the one hardware term a
#                 knob shares symmetry with) optimised on d90 -- `plan_probe.py --ceos`. Ronchigram flatness ignored.
#                 4 A where reachable (40 mrad), else the smallest d90. A5 and A4 have no partner knob: they set the
#                 floor, 25 A at 70 mrad from A5 alone. Rows needing a wider scan say so: pass WIN/STEP per submission.
#   ceos_a<A>     the operator retunes only C1/C3 and leaves every other term where the 30 mrad tuning put it
#                 ("as built", the first version of this sweep). Kept as the no-retune comparison.
# The wall: from ~70 mrad no scan field the 70 A box can host is 1.5x the probe (Rule 4), and a real detector would
# need ~1000+ px across to hold the Ronchigram. nl is ignored by run_thin_atomfind (Nyquist over the full box).
